t: That moneys of the American National Red Cross, District of Columbia Chapter, available for the construction of the aforesaid building, including any amount administratively determined necessary for the payment of salaries and expenses of personnel engaged upon the preparation of plans and specifications, field supervision, and general office expenses, may be transferred to and expended by the Public Buildings Administration of the Federal Works Agency, and such funds may be consolidated in the books of the Treasury Department into a special account for direct expenditure in the prosecution of said work, and the Commissioner of Public Buildings is authorized to prepare drawings and specifications for this building prior to the approval by the Attorney General of the title to such acquisition.

fable.w: The section only authorizes Red Cross funds to be transferred to and spent by a federal agency for construction, and lets the Commissioner of Public Buildings prepare drawings before the Attorney General approves title. The tempting reading is that the Red Cross chapter, an outside entity, is involved, but it merely supplies money and is not consulted on any federal decision. The Attorney General's title approval is an intra-federal step, so no outside party takes part in a federal decision.
fable.s: may be transferred to and expended by the Public Buildings Administration of the Federal Works Agency

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the transfer of funds from a non-federal entity (Red Cross) to a federal agency (Public Buildings Administration) for construction purposes. It also authorizes a federal official (Commissioner of Public Buildings) to prepare specifications before another federal official (Attorney General) approves the title. There is no requirement for consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in the decision-making process; the interaction is purely administrative and financial between the government and the donor, or internal to the government.
qwen_block.s: That moneys of the American National Red Cross, District of Columbia Chapter, available for the construction of the aforesaid building... may be transferred to and expended by the Public Buildings Administration of the Federal Works Agency... and the Commissioner of Public Buildings is authorized to prepare drawings and specifications for this building prior to the approval by the Attorney General of the title to such acquisition.

opus.w: This provision only covers moving the Red Cross chapter's construction funds to a federal agency and accounting for them. It also lets the Commissioner of Public Buildings prepare plans before the Attorney General approves the title. The Red Cross supplies money but is not consulted on, and cannot object to, a federal decision. The Attorney General's approval is coordination between federal officials, so it is not participation either. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue is created.
opus.s: moneys of the American National Red Cross, District of Columbia Chapter, available for the construction of the aforesaid building, including any amount administratively determined necessary for the payment of salaries and expenses of personnel engaged upon the preparation of plans and specifications, field supervision, and general office expenses, may be transferred to and expended by the Public Buildings Administration of the Federal Works Agency
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** The American National Red Cross chapter is outside the federal government, and the Attorney General must approve the title. That might look like an outside party and a formal approval step in a federal decision.

**Why it fails:** The Red Cross chapter only provides money. Its funds "may be transferred to and expended by" the Public Buildings Administration. Nothing lets it advise on or object to how the agency designs or builds the building. The Attorney General's title approval is one federal official acting on another agency's work, so it stays inside the government.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the transfer and expenditure of funds from the American National Red Cross by a federal agency. It does not require the federal government to consult with the Red Cross or any other outside party before making a decision. The Red Cross is providing funds, not participating in the decision-making process through consultation, advisory roles, or public comment. The only approval mentioned is by the Attorney General, who is inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: That moneys of the American National Red Cross, District of Columbia Chapter, available for the construction of the aforesaid building... may be transferred to and expended by the Public Buildings Administration of the Federal Works Agency
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the American National Red Cross is an outside entity participating in the decision to build the facility because its funds are used and its personnel are involved in preparation. However, the Red Cross is not consulting with the government to influence a federal decision; rather, the government is authorized to spend the Red Cross's money. The Red Cross is acting more like a grantor or funder, and the text describes administrative procedures for fund transfer and expenditure, not a participatory decision-making process involving outside input on policy or regulatory decisions. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this is closer to a funding arrangement than participation. Furthermore, the only "approval" mentioned is by the Attorney General (inside government) regarding title, which is intra-governmental.
